messages.subject: Error message part 5
parts:
Hi,

I have been running GGIR for about 130 GT3X-files with the script below. 
For two of the files I get an error message for part 5 looking like this:

Part 5 Busy processing ... see C:/Users/GGIR/meta/ms5.out for progress Errors and warnings for ID21.gt3x.RData$message [1] "NA/NaN argument" $call 1:dummywake Errors and warnings for ID115.gt3x.RData$message [1] "NA/NaN argument" $call 1:dummywake


Do you know wat this error code mean, and why only 2 of my 130 files get this error? And do you have any suggestion for solution?


Regards Kristina


The script I have used:

library(GGIR)

GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),

     datadir="C:/Users/…/ActiGraph to test GGIR",

     outputdir="C:/Users/…/GGIR ",

     do.report=c(2,4,5),

     overwrite=TRUE,

     #=====================

     # Part 2

     #=====================

     data_masking_strategy = 1, data_masking_strategy = 1 means select data based on hrs.del.start and hrs.del.end.

     hrs.del.start = 0, 

     hrs.del.end = 0,    

     maxdur = 0,         

     includedaycrit = c(0,0), 

     qwindow=c(0,24),   

     mvpathreshold =c(69),

     minimum_MM_length.part5 = 10,

     nonwear_approach = "2013",   

     #=====================

     # Part 3 + 4

     #=====================

     def.noc.sleep = 1,   

     outliers.only = FALSE,

     criterror = 4,       

     do.visual = TRUE,    

     save_ms5rawlevels = TRUE,

     save_ms5raw_without_invalid = FALSE,

     HASPT.algo = "NotWorn",

     HASIB.algo = "NotWorn",

     do.imp = FALSE,

     HASPT.ignore.invalid = NA,

     ignorenonwear = FALSE,

     relyonguider = TRUE,

     includenightcrit = 0,

     #=====================

     # Part 5

     #=====================

     threshold.lig = c(15),  

     threshold.mod = c(69), 

     includedaycrit.part5 = 2, 

     #=====================

     # Visual report

     #=====================

     timewindow = c("MM"),  

     visualreport=TRUE)

parts:
Hello Vincent, 

I am experiencing this same error argument for one gt3x file in part 5 as well. My code is below. I have examined this ID using read.gt3x R package and using the ActiLife software and there should be multiple days of valid data; it looks like this participant wore the device for 5 complete days. Idle sleep mode was not enabled for this study, so that is not a concern. The quality control plots also look normal for this participant. The only unique thing I have noticed with this cohort of participants (N~230) is there are more non-compliance in wear time than other studies I have ran using GGIR, but this participant in particular seems to have multiple days of valid data. 

Thank you in advance!
